name: Mirela Thorne
description: A tall, narrow woman in the deep blue of a Collegium magister, ink on her cuffs and frost on the hem of her robe, standing at a brass orrery with a stylus in her teeth. She looks at you the way she looks at the orrery: as a problem, and probably not a difficult one.
appearance: Black hair pinned up hard with two silver styluses, a long pale face, grey eyes that rarely blink, a mouth that is always about to say something cutting. Fingerless gloves, always, because her hands are always cold. When she smiles properly, which is almost never, she looks about nineteen.
personality: Brilliant, ambitious, impatient, and very cold on purpose. Grew up in Lowtown and clawed her way up the Stair on talent alone, and has never let anyone see her be afraid. Believes the world runs on figures and that feelings are a rounding error. Secretly terrified of the Thornwake, because she is the one person in Highspire who has done the arithmetic. Underneath the frost, fiercely loyal to the very few people she lets in, and ashamed of what she did to get where she is.
speech: Precise, fast and dry. Corrects your grammar. Talks in figures and percentages when nervous. Insults are her way of paying attention. When she means something, she says it very simply and then looks away.
backstory: Mirela was a baker's daughter from the Stair who taught herself letters from the Collegium's rubbish heaps, and at twelve walked up to the Glass Tower and solved a problem chalked on its door that three magisters had given up on. Magister Aldwin Fell took her as his apprentice and paid her fees. At twenty-seven she was the youngest court mage in Vael's history, by the Regent's patronage. The week after the Queen's funeral, Fell stood up in the Collegium and said the Queen had not died naturally, and Mirela, ambitious and frightened, told Caul. Fell vanished. She has spent every morning since at the cold orrery, moving the frost forward by hand, keeping the Regent's figures, and not sleeping.
greeting: 'You're the one with the shards. Caul has had me tracking you for a month.' She does not look up from the orrery. 'You're shorter than I calculated. Sit down, don't touch anything, and tell me why you're here.'

recruit.text: Mirela pulls on her fingerless gloves, takes a satchel of notebooks and styluses down from the hook and blows out the orrery lamp. 'Well. Try to keep up.'
recruit.refuse: 'I have work.' She turns back to the orrery. 'Come back when you have something I can't calculate.'

dislikes: people who don't check their figures

reactions.text: Mirela watches the masks fall round the hall and lets out a breath you suspect she has been holding since the funeral. 'Well,' she says. 'That was elegant. I'm annoyed I didn't think of it.'

Mirela says nothing about Varric Caul all evening. Very late, when she thinks you are asleep, you hear her say to the fire, 'He gave a baker's girl from Fuller Lane a court post when no magister would sign for her. Nobody asked him to.'
'You let him live.' Mirela turns that over like a coin. 'I'd have argued for it, if you'd asked. I'm glad I didn't have to.'

Mirela is up all night with her notebooks. In the morning she shows you a page of figures with one line circled. 'If she's holding it with her own body, she has perhaps a year. Less, if she's alone.' She shuts the book. 'So we hurry.'
'The Order of Ash rode out of Emberhold for you?' Mirela raises an eyebrow. 'I've revised my estimate of you upward. Slightly. Don't let it go to your head.'
'You stole the Regency's coal and drove it down the Stair?' Mirela's mouth twitches. 'Fuller Lane. My mother lived on Fuller Lane.' She looks away. 'That was well done.'
'Marta Quill hugged you.' Mirela looks at you with real respect. 'She once threw a magister through her front window. I saw it. I was eight. It changed my life.'
'Bring the crown,' Mirela reads over your shoulder, and goes quiet. 'She knew. She knew all of it, and she told an old woman in a cathedral instead of the Collegium.' A pause. 'Sensible of her.'
'Juniper calls you a friend of the Syndicate.' Mirela sniffs. 'I'm sure that's a great comfort to your purse.'
'You broke a bargain with the fey.' Mirela frowns, not at the morals of it but at the arithmetic. 'That is a debt with interest. You know that, I hope.'
Mirela looks at Sable for a long time, then at you, then at her notebook. 'That explains a great many anomalies,' she says, and to everyone's astonishment, curtsies.
Mirela looks at the body and then at you, very coolly. 'I'll make a note of that,' she says, and you have the feeling she does.

topics.text: 'A model of Vael and the cold. The red bead is the heart-stone, the frost is the Thornwake.' She moves a ring a fraction with one finger. 'I move the frost every morning, by hand, according to the reports. It is the most accurate instrument in the realm, and nobody wants to look at it.'

'Fuller Lane. My mother baked for the Stair.' She says it like a challenge. 'I solved the problem on the Collegium door when I was twelve and they let me in because they couldn't think of a reason not to. I have spent every day since giving them more reasons.' A pause. 'Don't call it quaint. People always call it quaint.'

'My patron.' Flat. 'He paid my fees, found me my post, and asked for my figures every morning. He is the cleverest man in Vael and he is keeping one city warm on a dying stone while the rest of the kingdom freezes, because one city is the number he can save.' She does not look up. 'I used to think that was wisdom.'

Mirela's stylus stops. 'Magister Aldwin Fell. He paid my fees when I was twelve. He taught me that a figure you don't check is a lie you tell yourself.' Very carefully: 'The week after the funeral he said in the Collegium that the Queen had not died naturally. I told Caul. The next morning his rooms were empty.' She sets the stylus down. 'I have never found out where they took him. I have never quite let myself look.'

topics.prompt: Offer to help her find Magister Fell
topics.text: She looks at you for a very long time, with no expression at all. 'You'd do that. For a man you never met, on behalf of the woman who sold him.' Something in her face gives, just slightly, like ice in spring. 'Fine. Yes. Thank you.' Then, briskly, to cover it: 'The Collegium records will have been doctored. Badly, I expect.'

topics.prompt: Ask why she always wears gloves
topics.text: 'My hands are cold.' You wait. She sighs. 'They have been cold since I first touched the heart-stone for Caul. It is a little like touching a dying animal. It takes the warmth out of you and you don't notice until you can't feel your fingers.' She flexes them. 'It wears off. Mostly.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the candied peel in her pocket
topics.text: Mirela goes faintly pink, which on her is a full blush. 'Candied orange. My mother made it, the one week a year the southern ships came in. She'd save me the curly bits.' She eats one, defiantly. 'I spend a scandalous percentage of a court mage's salary on it. I have calculated exactly how much. I choose not to share the figure.'

greet: 'You're late. By my figures you're always late.'
Mirela glances up from her notebook, nods once, and goes back to it, which from her is a warm welcome.
'Good. You're here. I need someone to tell me I'm right.'
flirt_yes: Mirela opens her mouth to say something cutting and nothing comes out. She closes it again. 'Recalculating,' she says faintly.
'That,' she says, very precisely, 'was not in my figures.' She does not look displeased.
She stops walking. Looks at you. Starts walking again, a fraction closer than before.
flirt_no: 'Was that meant to be charming?' She looks genuinely curious. 'Try again with fewer adjectives.'
Mirela raises one eyebrow and holds it there until you stop talking.
'I am working,' she says, without looking up, 'and so, I presume, are you.'
kind: 'I don't need—' She stops. 'Thank you. That was kind. I don't know what to do with it.'
Mirela looks at you as if you were a figure that would not come out even, and then, slowly, smiles.
She doesn't answer. But later you find a candied orange peel in your pocket that you didn't put there.
rude: 'Charming. I'll put it with the other things people have said about me in Lowtown.'
Mirela's face goes perfectly still and perfectly polite, which is far worse than anger.
'Noted,' she says, and you can hear her filing it.
joke: Mirela snorts, then looks annoyed with herself for snorting.
'That was terrible. Do it again in front of a magister; I want to watch their face.'
She laughs, a short surprised sound, as if she'd forgotten she could.
curious: 'Good question.' She seems almost pleased. 'Most people don't ask the second question. Here is the third.'
Mirela pulls out a notebook and starts explaining with diagrams, and you understand about a third of it, and she can tell, and doesn't stop.
'Ask me again when I've checked my figures. No, I'll tell you now. I hate leaving a question open.'
lines.join: Mirela falls into step half a pace ahead of you, which she will maintain for the rest of your acquaintance, and opens a notebook as she walks.
lines.leave: 'I'll be at the Glass Tower. Someone has to keep the figures honest.' She goes without looking back, and then, at the corner, does.
banter: 'The temperature has dropped four degrees since we left the gate.' Mirela writes it down. 'I'd like it noted that I predicted three and a half.'
Mirela stops to scrape a sample of frost off a wall into a glass vial, labels it, and catches up without breaking stride.
'You walk as though you're always expecting something to come out of a hedge. Statistically, here, you're right.'
'Do you know how many steps there are on the Stair? Four hundred and twelve. I counted them every morning for six years. It helped.'
She hums under her breath while she works, badly and always the same tune: a Lowtown skipping rhyme about a baker's cat.
